summary: PSI 53/70 decomposes exactly (score.py reproduces 14/14 reports). Mobile lost points: LCP 23, TBT 15, FCP 5.4, SI 3.5. Desktop: TBT 26.4 of 30. Lantern facts (source-verified): module chunks that finish before observed FCP/LCP always count, so mobile FCP≈0.9s+5.1ms/KB and LCP≈0.9s+6ms/KB of the ~800 KB pre-LCP set (boot JS 554 KB is 70% of it). Document TTFB is not simulated and hurts only SI (×1.4 observed SI). TBT is threshold-convex: fixture mobile CPU ×2/×4/×8 gives 67/356/1443 ms, desktop ×4 gives 444 ms; post-FCP CPU −50% or tasks ≤12 ms gives 0–78 ms. Projected: TBT fix alone → 66/95; plus byte diet → 73–85; plus boot-after-LCP → 91–95 mobile. Mobile 85 needs pre-LCP set ≤300 KB AND TBT ≤200–250; desktop 95 needs TBT ≤110 ms on a ~4× slower CPU.

findings.claim: Every High-priority module chunk that finished before the observed paint stays in Lantern's FCP and LCP graphs. Modules emit no EvaluateScript with a URL, so Lantern cannot prove they are non-blocking. Mobile FCP/LCP are therefore a linear function of the bytes in that set (≈5.1 ms/KB FCP, ≈6 ms/KB LCP at 1.6 Mb/s); CPU before FCP is under 2% of FCP.

findings.claim: Document TTFB is not simulated: Lantern uses the per-origin median server time, 238 ms in prod instead of the 2 750 ms MISS. TTFB reaches the score only through Speed Index = max(FCP, 1.4·observedSI + 0.4·layoutSI) on mobile and 0.575/0.49 on desktop. That is the whole SI 7.1 s (local MISS) vs 4.9 s (PSI) anomaly. MISS→HIT is worth ≈+2.6 mobile / +1.3 desktop vs PSI-now, and a full Prague-like MISS costs −3.4 / −4.8.

Same-origin static-asset server latency (Lantern origin median) is a real lever. 19→238 ms costs desktop FCP +219/LCP +339 ms (−3 to −4 pts) and mobile +219/+294 (−1 pt). Production measured 238 ms from Prague.

changes.title: Pre-LCP byte budget as a CI ratchet (requests issued before LCP: doc + CSS + fonts + hero + modulepreload/Link JS)
changes.mechanism: Lantern LCP ≈ 0.9 s + 6 ms/KB × the pre-LCP set (mobile). Add a single 'preLcpTransferBytes' metric (brotli of doc + render-blocking CSS + preloaded fonts + LCP image + every High JS preloaded or statically imported before boot). Ratchet it toward ≤300 KB. Remove stray route modulepreloads from the Link header (admin.analytics, blog.index, Footnotes, headings, useInFeedAds, prepareContent, eventInvoiceMath, PaginatedPostGrid).
changes.expected_effect: Each −100 KB gives ≈−0.5 s FCP/−0.6 s LCP mobile and −0.08 s desktop. The full byte diet (≈−300 KB) gives fixture 65→83 (+post50: 88); PSI 53→73 (gap persists) or 85 (gap collapses), together with LA-C1.

changes.mechanism: Requests that start after the observed LCP are excluded from the Lantern FCP/LCP graphs (FirstContentfulPaint.js:104). Inline loader: a PerformanceObserver('largest-contentful-paint') first entry plus rAF, or the first input, or 1.5 s triggers import(entry) and injects modulepreloads. B-lite (Low priority) removes JS from the FCP set only (FCP −2.6 s) and leaves LCP unchanged. The hero element must not be re-created or repainted larger by hydration, or obs LCP moves after JS.
changes.expected_effect: Fixture alone 65→78 (FCP 3974→1367, LCP 4819→2117, TBT 356→885). With LA-C1: 92–95 mobile and 99–100 desktop@cpu4. PSI projection with W1: mobile 91–95, desktop ~96.

changes.title: Hero-first HTML: move the LCP hero ahead of the 103 KB header payload (header <style> blocks and mega-menu markup after main, or deferred)
changes.mechanism: The hero sits at byte 177 712 of 569 347. On slow PSI hosts the hero paints in a later frame than FCP, and the paint can slip past DCL, which pulls the post-boot wave into the LCP set (the PSI 3.5 s FCP→LCP gap vs 0.85–1.9 s elsewhere). Getting the hero into the first paint makes obs LCP equal obs FCP.
changes.expected_effect: Removes up to ~1.6 s of PSI-only LCP gap (+6–13 pts mobile depending on the other waves); no effect on the fixture or the M3.
changes.estimate_basis: PSI LCP 6.6 s ⇒ ≈930 KB set vs ≈800 KB head set (6 ms/KB); M3 and fixture obs LCP = FCP frame
changes.risk_notes: Visual order and CSS for the header must be preserved (CLS 0 must hold); SSR chrome parity.
changes.verification: Capture a PSI JSON after deploy: observedLargestContentfulPaint − observedFirstContentfulPaint < 100 ms and < observedDomContentLoaded.

changes.title: Static-asset and media edge latency (origin median server time 238 ms in prod)
changes.mechanism: Lantern applies the origin median server response to every same-origin request. Serving /assets/* from the edge cache without invoking the Worker and caching /media variants at the edge lowers the median.
changes.expected_effect: 238→~50 ms: desktop +3–4 pts (LCP −0.3 s), mobile +1 pt.
changes.risk_notes: Needs a production check of cf-cache-status and server-timing on /assets.

My h1→h2 what-if confirms the size (−940 ms FCP, +6 perf on mobile). The desktop cpu×4 profile (LA-C6) and the preLcpTransferBytes metric (LA-C3) should be added there, not duplicated.

boot-js / lcp-path: fixes that reduce FCP (B-lite fetchpriority=low, byte diets) raise TBT through the FCP-anchored window (fixture TBT 356→873–885). Sequence them after hydration (LA-C1) or measure together.

server-cache: TTFB/MISS work moves only SI in Lantern (doc TTFB is not simulated); its FCP/LCP effect comes through the static-asset origin median (LA-C7). Claims of FCP/LCP gains from document caching should be checked against this.
css: render-blocking CSS savings do not appear while boot JS is in the FCP set (CSS −70% gives FCP 0 ms, LCP −225 ms). The CSS diet pays off for FCP after LA-C4.
hydration: owns LA-C1's code; my numbers set the target (tasks ≤12 ms obs at sandbox ×4; post-FCP CPU −50%).
open_questions: PSI lighthouseResult JSON is needed (machine with egress): obs LCP vs obs DCL, LCP element, bytes ended before obs LCP, network-server-latency per origin, long-tasks list. It decides whether the 3.5 s PSI FCP→LCP gap is a late paint (LA-C5) or a different LCP element (e.g. consent text).
Why do the PSI mobile and desktop samples imply ~3–5× different host speeds? More PSI samples (≥5 per form) or CrUX/LHCI on the deployed URL are needed before tuning against desktop 740 ms.
Does PSI (US datacenters) get a consent decision or region behaviour that loads gtag earlier than in Prague runs (gtagLoadPolicy (b))?
Is the 238 ms origin median for /assets in prod an edge MISS or Worker invocation? Check cf-cache-status and server-timing for /assets/*.js and /media/*.
